evaluations.label: Stall recovery, worst of 3
evaluations.sentence: After the 10.00 s outage the player stalled for 4.10 s in its worst of 3 runs; the limit is <= 14.00 s.

evaluations.label: Latency restored after the stall, worst of 3
evaluations.sentence: Latency was not back within 10.00 s in 2 runs of 3, after at least 65.08 s of observation; the limit is <= 60.00 s. It stood at 10.15 s when the observation ended, 4.08 s further behind than before the outage (6.07 s), against a maximum of 10.00 s.

evaluations.label: Latency at its own level, worst of 3
evaluations.sentence: Latency was not back within 2.00 s of its own level before the outage in 3 runs of 3, after at least 65.08 s of observation; the limit is <= 60.00 s. It stood at 8.96 s when the observation ended, 2.89 s further behind than before the outage (6.07 s).
evaluations.note: The absolute limit and the relative reading disagree: run 1 was back within the 10.00 s of the policy and not back within 2.00 s of its own level of 6.07 s. Which of the two separates a player that came back from one that did not is chosen from the measured values (docs/decisions/readiness.md, ADR-153); the verdict is the absolute one.

configurations.label: A plus streaming.liveSync.enabled
configurations.hypothesis: Shaka 5.3.3's `streaming.liveSync` (off by default) holds the playhead near the live edge by changing the playback rate: when the distance from `seekRange().end` to the playhead exceeds `targetLatency + targetLatencyTolerance` (0.5 s + 0.5 s by default) it plays at `maxPlaybackRate` (1.1) until it is back. After a 10 s origin outage the defaults leave the playhead 4 s further behind the edge for good (docs/decisions/e2e-rec.md), which is above the 10 s latency maximum; with live sync on, the playhead gains 0.1 s per second and latency is back under the maximum within seconds. Expected: PB-RDY-003 shows GO for the restore line; PB-RDY-001, 002 and 004 stay GO (a healthy join sits within a second of `seekRange().end`, so the rate stays 1). Rejected if latency is not restored within the limit, or if the healthy checks regress (a sustained rate above 1 on a healthy stream, a longer join).
